'''De'Aaron Martez Fox''' (born December 20, 1997) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[San Antonio Spurs]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]] before being selected fifth overall by the [[Sacramento Kings]] in the [[2017 NBA draft]]. Fox had a breakout season in [[2022–23 NBA season|2023]], earning his first [[NBA All-Star Game|All-Star selection]], an [[All-NBA Team]] nod, and was named [[NBA Clutch Player of the Year]] while leading the Kings to their first postseason berth since [[2005–06 Sacramento Kings season|2006]]. He also [[List of NBA annual steals leaders|led the league in steals]] in 2024. Traded to the Spurs at the 2025 trade deadline, Fox earned his second All-Star selection in 2026 and reached the [[2026 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]] with the team later that season.

==Early life==
[[File:20160330 MCDAAG De'Aaron Fox dribbling.jpg|191px|thumb|right|Fox at the [[2016 McDonald's All-American Game]]]]
Fox attended [[Cypress Lakes High School]] in [[Cypress, Texas]].<ref>{{cite web|title=De'aaron Fox|url=https://247sports.com/Player/DeAaron-Fox-23975|website=247 Sports|access-date=March 30, 2018}}</ref> As a junior, he averaged 23.8 points, 6.1 rebounds, and 3.5 assists per game. During the summer, Fox played for Houston Hoops in the [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League]] Circuit (EYBL) where he earned EYBL first-team honors.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.d1circuit.com/news_article/show/530622-1st-team-all-eybl|title=1st Team All-EYBL|date=July 2, 2015|publisher=D1 Circuit|access-date=July 2, 2015}}</ref> On November 29, Fox scored 31 points, 12 rebounds, and 6 assists in a 68–53 victory over [[MacArthur High School (Irving, Texas)|MacArthur]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://usatodayhss.com/2015/top-guards-deaaron-fox-andrew-jones-put-on-show-at-thanksgiving-hoopfest|title=Top guards De'Aaron Fox, Andrew Jones put on a show at Thanksgiving Hoopfest|last=Barnett|first=Ja|date=November 29, 2015|publisher=USA Today High School Sports|access-date=November 30, 2015}}</ref> On December 28, Fox put up 31 points and 6 assists in a 91–81 victory against [[Jay M. Robinson High School]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.highschoolot.com/fox-spartans-get-first-hsot-win/15200877/|title=Fox, Spartans get first HSOT win|date=December 28, 2015|publisher=High School OT|access-date=December 28, 2015}}</ref> As a senior, Fox averaged 32.1 points, 7.6 rebounds, and 4.1 assists per game.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://usatodayhss.com/2016/gatorade-national-poy-watch-deaaron-fox|title=Cypress Lakes guard De'Aaron Fox still has business to finish before heading off to Kentucky|date=March 24, 2016|publisher=USA Today High School Sports|access-date=March 24, 2016}}</ref> In January 2016, Fox was named a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] and played in the [[2016 McDonald's All-American Game]] on March 30. In April, Fox played in the 2016 [[Jordan Brand Classic]], leading the East team to a 131–117 win while earning Co-MVP honors alongside Kentucky teammate [[Malik Monk]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://usatodayhss.com/2016/future-kentucky-wildcats-guards-deaaron-fox-malik-monk-share-mvp-at-jordan-brand-classic|title=Fox, Monk share MVP honors at 2016 Jordan Brand Classic|date=April 15, 2016|work=USA Today HSS|access-date=March 30, 2018}}</ref> Fox then competed at the [[Nike Hoop Summit]] Games. He made the 2015–16 USA Men's Basketball Men's Junior Team in September 2015.<ref name=ukathletics>{{cite web|url=http://ukathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=680|title=De' Aaron Fox bio|date=August 10, 2017 |access-date=March 30, 2018}}</ref> He was also invited to the NBPA Top 100 camp. Throughout his high school career, Fox led Cypress Lakes to three state playoff appearances including a regional final appearance his senior year, and twice scored 50 points in a single game.

During his high school years in the Houston area, Fox also played on the AAU circuit with Houston Hoops ; he was teammates with future NBA players including [[Justin Jackson (basketball, born 1995)|Justin Jackson]], [[Justise Winslow]] and [[Kelly Oubre Jr.]]. Fox and Jackson, who grew up in the same region, developed a close relationship through years of youth and AAU basketball before later following different collegiate paths.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=25 December 2025 |author=Jenny Dial Creech |date=22 June 2017 |language=en |title=Boyhood friends De'Aaron Fox, Justin Jackson are teammates again |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/sports/rockets/article/Boyhood-friends-De-Aaron-Fox-Justin-11233512.php |website=Houston Chronicle}}<!-- auto-translated from French by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

In the class of 2016, Fox was the nation's second-best point guard behind [[Lonzo Ball]]. He was rated as a five-star recruit and ranked the consensus No. 6 overall recruit by the three main recruiting services: [[Rivals.com|Rivals]], [[ESPNU Recruiting Insider|ESPN]], and [[247Sports.com|247Sports]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2016/de-aaron-fox-434|title=De'Aaron Fox, 2016 Point guard|website=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]]|access-date=November 24, 2021|archive-date=November 24, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211124233211/https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2016/de-aaron-fox-434|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/185292/deaaron-fox|title=De'Aaron Fox – Basketball Recruiting – Player Profiles|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=November 23, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://247sports.com/Player/DeAaron-Fox-23975/high-school-38455/|title=De'Aaron Fox, Cypress Lakes, Point guard|publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]]|access-date=November 23, 2021}}</ref>

He committed to Kentucky over [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]], Arizona, and [[LSU Tigers basketball|LSU]] on November 12, 2015, live on [[ESPNU]]. With his reason to choose UK he stated "It felt like a family<ref>{{cite news |id={{ProQuest|1732684486}} |last1=Ellis |first1=Josh |title=De'Aaron Fox commits to UK |agency=University Wire |date=12 November 2015 }}</ref> (at UK)".<ref name="DFcommit">{{Cite web |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |date=November 12, 2015 |title=Point guard De'Aaron Fox, No. 7 in ESPN 100, chooses Kentucky |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/14115542/deaaron-fox-no-7-espn-100-commits-kentucky-wildcats |access-date=March 30, 2018 |website=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref>

==College career==
On November 13, 2016, Fox recorded 21 points and 3 assists during a 93–69 victory over [[Canisius College]] at the Bluegrass Showcase. Six days later, he posted 16 points and 6 assists to defeat [[Duquesne University]], 93–69. In a game against [[Arizona State]] on November 28, he recorded a triple double with 14 points, 11 rebounds, and 10 assists; this made Fox only the second Wildcat in the history of Kentucky basketball to record one after Chris Mill in 1988.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.seccountry.com/kentucky/kentucky-basketball-deaaron-fox-records-the-storied-programs-elusive-second-triple-double|title=Kentucky Basketball: De'Aaron Fox records the storied program's elusive second triple-double|website=seccountry.com|author=Kyle Tucker|date=November 29, 2016|access-date=March 30, 2018}}</ref> On January 7, 2017, Fox scored 27 points to go along with 6 assists in a 97–71 victory over [[Arkansas University|Arkansas]]. He tallied 21 points and 5 assists to defeat [[Mississippi State]], 88–81, on January 17. On February 18 that year, Fox scored 16 points and dished out 5 assists to help the Wildcats defeat the [[Georgia Bulldogs]]. On March 4, Fox scored 19 points in a 71–63 win over [[Texas A&M]]. Kentucky would go on to defeat [[Georgia Bulldogs|Georgia]] in the quarterfinals and [[University of Alabama|Alabama]] in the semi-finals. On March 12, Fox scored 18 points in an 82–65 win over [[Arkansas University|Arkansas]] in the [[2017 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]] in addition earning SEC Tournament MVP honors.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/college/2017/03/12/live-sec-final-updates-kentucky-vs-arkansas/99091070/|title=Kentucky beats Arkansas for SEC title|last=Ammenheuser|first=David|date=March 12, 2017|publisher=Tennessean|access-date=March 12, 2017}}</ref> On March 17, Fox scored 19 points and 3 assists to defeat [[Northern Kentucky University]] in the first round of the [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. On March 19, Fox scored 14 points to defeat [[Wichita State University|Wichita State]] 65–62 in the second round of the NCAA Tournament. On March 24, In a Sweet 16 matchup against the [[UCLA Bruins]], Fox scored 39 points to advance the [[Kentucky Wildcats]] to the Elite Eight game.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2017/03/25/kentucky-ucla-ncaa-tournament-deaaron-fox|title=De'Aaron Fox gets best of Lonzo Ball as Kentucky advances to Elite Eight|last=Rosenberg|first=Michael|date=March 25, 2017|magazine=Sports Illustrated|access-date=March 30, 2018}}</ref> In the Elite Eight, Fox only scored 13 points in the regional final,, while North Carolina forward [[Justin Jackson (basketball, born 1995)|Justin Jackson]] led the Tar Heels in scoring with 19 points. North Carolina secured a 75–73 victory on a last-second jumper by [[Luke Maye]].<ref>{{cite web
 | title = North Carolina 75–73 Kentucky – Recap
 | url = https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400948726
 | publisher = ESPN
 | access-date = 25 December 2025
}}</ref>

At the conclusion of his freshman season, Fox announced that he would forgo his final three years of collegiate eligibility and enter the [[2017 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/nba-draft-2017-kentuckys-deaaron-fox-will-go-pro-sign-with-an-agent/|title=NBA Draft 2017: Kentucky's De'Aaron Fox will go pro, sign with an agent|department=[[CBS Sports]]|agency=[[CBS]]|author=Kyle Boone|date=April 3, 2017|access-date=March 30, 2018}}</ref> As he stated in his announcement, "I think I’ve had a pretty good freshman season through the guidance of our coaching staff and I think it’s time for me to live out my dream."<ref>{{cite news |id={{ProQuest|1883350012}} |title=De'Aaron Fox declares for the NBA Draft |agency=University Wire |date=3 April 2017 }}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Sacramento Kings (2017–2025)===

====Early years (2017–2019)====
On June 22, 2017, Fox was selected with the fifth overall pick in the [[2017 NBA draft]] by the [[Sacramento Kings]]. The team also selected former teammate [[Justin Jackson (basketball, born 1995)|Justin Jackson]] in the same round.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=25 December 2025 |author=Jenny Dial Creech |date=22 June 2017 |language=en |title=Boyhood friends De'Aaron Fox, Justin Jackson are teammates again |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/sports/rockets/article/Boyhood-friends-De-Aaron-Fox-Justin-11233512.php |website=Houston Chronicle}}<!-- auto-translated from French by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

On July 8, 2017, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Kings.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-fox-jackson-giles/|title=Kings sign #5 overall pick De'Aaron Fox|date=July 8, 2017|work=NBA.com|access-date=March 30, 2018}}</ref> During four games of the [[2017 NBA Summer League]], Fox averaged 11.8 points, 3 assists and 2.3 steals while playing 21.3 minutes per game. Fox made his NBA debut for the Kings in their season opener on October 18, 2017, against the [[Houston Rockets]], where he scored 14 points, 4 rebounds, and 5 assist in 24-plus minutes in a 105–100 loss.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/ex-cats/article179703026.html|title=De'Aaron Fox stole the show in NBA debut|last=Voisin|first=Ailene|date=October 19, 2017|work=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]]|access-date=March 30, 2018}}</ref> On October 23, 2017, Fox recorded a career-high 19 points, 4 assist, 5 rebounds, and 3 steals in a 117–115 loss against the [[Phoenix Suns]]. On December 8, 2017, he scored 14 points, 4 assist and 2 steals in a 116–109 win against the [[New Orleans Pelicans]]. On January 6, 2018, Fox recorded 18 points and 7 assist in a 106–98 victory over the [[Denver Nuggets]]. On January 25, 2018, Fox scored 14 points, 4 assist and a putback [[slam dunk]] with 3.3 seconds left giving the [[Sacramento Kings]] the lead in an 89–88 win over the [[Miami Heat]]. On January 28, 2018, Fox scored a season-high 26 points, going 6–6 from three-point range in a 15-point loss to the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/201801280SAS.html|title=Sacramento Kings at San Antonio Spurs Box Score, January 28, 2018|access-date=May 27, 2018}}</ref> On February 14, Fox was named [[Lonzo Ball]]'s replacement for the [[Rising Stars Challenge]].

On November 1, 2018, during a 146–115 win over the Atlanta Hawks, Fox notched his first career triple-double with 31 points, 10 rebounds, and 15 assists to bring the Kings to a 6–3 record, becoming the only player after [[LeBron James]] in 2005 to score a 30-point triple double before the age of 21. Fox drastically improved during the 2018–2019 season. Not only did he improve in every major statistical category (Including his points per game from 11.6 to 17.3 and assists per game from 4.4 to 7.3), He also finished top 3 and was nominated for the NBA Most Improved Player Award, finishing second to [[Pascal Siakam]].

====Franchise player (2019–2022)====
On July 31, 2020, Fox scored a then career-high 39 points in a 129–120 loss to the [[San Antonio Spurs]]. This was the Kings’ first game in the [[2020 NBA Bubble|Orlando bubble]], returning from a 4-month hiatus due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/kings/kings-wasting-deaaron-foxs-career-high-vs-spurs-tough-swallow?amp|title=Kings wasting De'Aaron Fox's career high vs. Spurs 'tough to swallow'}}</ref>

On November 25, 2020, Fox signed a five-year, $163 million contract extension with the Kings.<ref>{{cite news|title=Kings Sign De'Aaron Fox To Contract Extension|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-deaaron-fox-contract-extension|date=November 25, 2020|work=NBA.com|access-date=December 4, 2020}}</ref> On February 8, 2021, Fox was named [[Western Conference (NBA)|Western Conference]] Player of the Week for the first time in his career averaging 31 points & nearly 9 assists while winning all 4 games on the first week of February. On March 26, 2021, Fox scored a then career-high 44 points on 16-of-22 from the field in a 141–119 victory over the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=De'Aaron Fox's career-high 44 more proof Kings guard becoming NBA star|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/deaaron-foxs-career-high-44-061457164.html|access-date=2021-03-26|website=sports.yahoo.com|language=en-US}}{{Dead link|date=January 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> On March 29, 2021, Fox was once again named Player of the Week for the second time during Week 14. Fox averaged nearly 37 points & 5 assists per game while shooting 64% from the field over the 4 games, all ending in victories for the Kings.<ref>{{Cite web|title=De'Aaron Fox, Terry Rozier named NBA Players of the Week|url=https://www.nba.com/news/nba-players-week-14-deaaron-fox-terry-rozier|access-date=2021-04-15|website=www.nba.com|language=en}}</ref>

On March 5, 2022, Fox tied his then career-high with 44 points on 18-for-31 shooting in a 114–113 loss against the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Finney-Smith, Dinwiddie help Mavs rally to edge Kings|url=https://www.nba.com/game/sac-vs-dal-0022100954|website=NBA.com |language=en |date=March 5, 2022}}</ref> On March 12, Fox had 41 points and a season-high 11 assists in a 134–125 loss against the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Clarkson drops career-high 45 as Jazz withstand Fox's 41|url=https://www.nba.com/game/sac-vs-uta-0022101010|website=NBA.com |language=en |date=March 13, 2022}}</ref>

====First All-Star and playoff appearance (2022–2023)====
On November 5, 2022, Fox put up 37 points, alongside a buzzer-beating, game-winning three, in a 126–123 overtime win over the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/kings-news-deaaron-fox-breaks-magic-heart-with-ruthless-logo-buzzer-beater-in-ot/|title=VIDEO: Kings star De'Aaron Fox breaks Magic's heart with ruthless logo buzzer-beater in OT|website=ClutchPoints|last=Guinhawa|first=Angelo|date=November 5, 2022|access-date=November 5, 2022}}</ref> He was named the Western Conference Player of the Week for November 14–20 after leading Sacramento to a 3–0 record, where he averaged 25 points, 3.7 rebounds and 8 assists per game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=De'Aaron Fox, Tyrese Haliburton named NBA Players of the Week |url=https://www.nba.com/news/nba-players-week-deaaron-fox-tyrese-haliburton |access-date=February 19, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On December 28, Fox recorded 31 points and a season-high 13 assists in a 127–126 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Monk scores 33, hits winning free throw as Kings top Nuggets|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401468677|website=ESPN.com. |language=en |date=December 28, 2022}}</ref> On February 10, 2023, he was named an [[NBA All-Star|All-Star]] for the first time in his career as a reserve. Fox and [[Anthony Edwards (basketball)|Anthony Edwards]] were announced as injury replacements for injured stars [[Stephen Curry]] and [[Zion Williamson]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Edwards, De'Aaron Fox and Pascal Siakam named as injury replacements for 2023 All-Star Game |url=https://www.nba.com/news/edwards-fox-siakam-all-star-injury-replacements |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 10, 2023 |date=February 10, 2023 }}</ref> On February 24, Fox recorded a season-high 42 points, 12 assists, five rebounds and five steals in a 176–175 double overtime win over the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. It was the [[List of highest-scoring NBA games|second-highest scoring game]] in NBA history.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kings outlast Clippers 176-175 in double overtime |url=https://www.espn.com.au/nba/recap/_/gameId/401469057 |website=ESPN |access-date=February 25, 2023 |date=February 24, 2023}}</ref> On March 15, Fox put up a game-winning three-pointer in a 117–114 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/kings-news-deaaron-fox-caps-wild-4th-quarter-with-dagger-3-to-stun-bulls|title=Kings star De'Aaron Fox caps wild 4th quarter with dagger 3 to stun Bulls|website=ClutchPoints|last=Pagaduan|first=Jedd|date=March 15, 2023|access-date=March 15, 2023}}</ref> 

In Game 1 of the Kings’ first round playoff series against the [[Golden State Warriors]], Fox put up 38 points in a 126–123 win. This was the second-most points in a playoff debut, after [[Luka Dončić]] who scored 42 points in 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://clutchpoints.com/kings-news-deaaron-fox-enters-playoff-pantheon-with-record-debut-only-topped-by-luka-doncic|title= Kings' De'Aaron Fox enters Playoff pantheon with record debut only topped by Luka Doncic|website=ClutchPoints|last=Guinhawa|first=Angelo|date=April 15, 2023|access-date=April 15, 2023}}</ref> On April 19, 2023, Fox was named as the inaugural recipient of the [[NBA Clutch Player of the Year Award]], winning over [[Jimmy Butler]] and [[DeMar DeRozan]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2022-23-kia-nba-clutch-player-of-the-year|title=De'Aaron Fox named 2022-23 Kia NBA Clutch Player of the Year|work=NBA.com|agency=Associated Press|date=April 19, 2023|access-date=April 20, 2023|last=Reynolds|first=Tim}}</ref> He averaged 27.4 points and 7.7 assists in the series, but he couldn't avoid the Warriors winning the series in 7 games.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nba.com/game/gsw-vs-sac-0042200167| title=CURRY'S 50-PT MASTERPIECE LIFTS WARRIORS IN GAME 7|work=NBA.com|date=May 1, 2023|last=McCauley|first=Janie}}</ref>

====Career high in scoring and steals leader (2023–2025)====
On November 17, 2023, Fox scored a season-high 43 points along with 8 rebounds and 7 assists in a 129–120 win over the San Antonio Spurs.<ref>{{cite web|title=Fox's season-high 43 leads Kings past Wembanyama, Spurs 129-120 in in-season tourney|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401584120|website=ESPN.com|date=November 18, 2023|access-date=November 18, 2023}}</ref> On December 2, Fox scored 26 points and recorded a career-high 16 assists in a 123–117 win over the Denver Nuggets.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kings overcome Jokic's 8th triple-double of the season, beat Nuggets 123-117|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401584918|website=ESPN.com|date=December 3, 2023|access-date=December 3, 2023}}</ref> On March 6, 2024, Fox tied his then career high with 44 points in a 130–120 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|title= De'Aaron Fox ties career high with 44 points as Kings roll to a 130-120 victory over Lakers|url= https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401585529 |website=ESPN.com|date=March 6, 2024|access-date= March 6, 2024}}</ref>

On November 15, 2024, Fox scored a career-high 60 points in a 130–126 overtime loss to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. His 60 points set a franchise record for the most points scored by a Kings player in a game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/kings-news-deaaron-fox-historic-60-loss-timberwolves|title=Kings star De'Aaron Fox's historic 60-burger goes down drain in loss to Timberwolves|website=ClutchPoints|last=Finnegan|first=Troy|date=November 15, 2024|access-date=November 15, 2024}}</ref> The very next day, Fox scored 49 points and delivered 9 assists in a 122–117 win over the Utah Jazz. He became the second Sacramento player to score at least 100 points in a two-game span, with the other being [[DeMarcus Cousins]] in 2016 when he scored 104. Fox is just the third player in NBA history to score at least 109 over two days, joining [[Kobe Bryant]] (2007) and [[Wilt Chamberlain]] (17 different times).<ref>{{cite web|title= De'Aaron Fox scores 49 as Sacramento Kings defeat Utah Jazz |url= https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/42438800/deaaron-fox-scores-49-sacramento-kings-defeat-utah-jazz |website=ESPN.com|date=November 16, 2024|access-date= November 16, 2024}}</ref>

===San Antonio Spurs (2025–present)===
On February 3, 2025, Fox was traded, alongside [[Jordan McLaughlin]], to the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in a three-team trade also involving the [[Chicago Bulls]] in which they sent [[Zach LaVine]], [[Sidy Cissoko]], three first-round picks and two second-round picks to the Kings. The Spurs sent [[Zach Collins]], [[Tre Jones]] and a 2025-first round pick to the Bulls, who also received [[Kevin Huerter]] from the Kings.<ref>{{Cite web |title=De'Aaron Fox headed to Spurs, Zach LaVine to Kings in 3-team trade {{!}} NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/news/deaaron-fox-trade-kings-spurs-bulls-zach-lavine-3-team-deal |access-date=2025-04-22 |website=NBA |language=en}}</ref>

On February 5, Fox made his debut for the Spurs, recording 24 points, five rebounds, 13 assists (matching his season-high) and three steals in a 126–125 win over the [[Atlanta Hawks]]. He became the first player in Spurs franchise history to post 20+ points and 10+ assists in a debut.<ref>{{cite web|title=De'Aaron Fox shines alongside Victor Wembanyama in Spurs debut|url=https://www.nba.com/news/deaaron-fox-spurs-debut|website=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2025|access-date=February 6, 2025}}</ref> In 17 appearances for San Antonio, Fox averaged 19.7 points, 4.3 rebounds, and 6.8 assists. On March 13, it was announced that Fox would undergo season-ending surgery to repair tendon damage in his left pinkie finger.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Spurs' De'Aaron Fox to have season-ending surgery on pinkie|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/44240292/sources-spurs-fox-season-ending-surgery-pinkie|access-date=April 4, 2025|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref> 

On August 4, the Spurs and Fox reached a 4-year, $229 million maximum contract extension. The max deal has no player option in the final year and will keep him with the franchise until the 2029–30 season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-08-04 |title=Agent: Spurs, Fox reach $229M max extension |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/45900046/spurs-deaaron-fox-reach-4-year-229m-max-extension-agent-says |access-date=2025-08-04 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> On February 12, 2026, Fox was announced to be the replacement for [[Giannis Antetokounmpo]] for the [[2026 NBA All-Star Game]], marking it as his second official All Star appearance since the [[2022–23 NBA season]].<ref>{{cite web |last=NBA.com News |title=De’Aaron Fox replaces Giannis Antetokounmpo in 2026 All-Star Game |url=https://www.nba.com/news/deaaron-fox-replaces-giannis-antetokounmpo-2026-all-star-game |website=[[NBA.com]] |publisher=NBA Media Ventures, LLC |date=February 12, 2026 |access-date=February 12, 2026}}</ref>

In Game 4 of the [[2026 NBA Finals]], Fox held the ball in a runout while the Spurs held a 106–105 lead. However, rather than dribbling out the clock as was expected, Fox attempted a layup, which was blocked by [[OG Anunoby]], allowing the [[New York Knicks]] to gain possession. After a missed 3-pointer from [[Jalen Brunson]], Anunoby achieved a tip-in to win the game at 107–106, completing a record 29-point comeback and giving the Knicks a 3–1 series lead over the Spurs.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49026753/wembanyama-spurs-resolute-game-4-collapse-knicks|title=Wembanyama, Spurs resolute after Game 4 collapse to Knicks|website=espn.com|last=Wright|first=Michael|date=June 13, 2026|access-date=June 13, 2026}}</ref> Fox's decision to attempt the layup was criticized as one of the biggest blunders in Finals history, drawing comparisons to [[J. R. Smith]] in Game 1 of the [[2018 NBA Finals]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=read |first=Rick Tidoy·2 min |date=2026-06-11 |title=“I’m Disgusted RN!”: Micah Parsons Doesn’t Hold Back After De’Aaron Fox’s Crucial Finals Blunder |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/m-disgusted-rn-micah-parsons-172559882.html |access-date=2026-06-15 |website=Yahoo Sports |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=read |first=Aikansh Chaudhary·2 min |date=2026-06-11 |title=NBA fans point out mistake ‘worse than JR Smith against the Warriors’ Spurs star made late in Game 4 |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/nba-fans-point-mistake-worse-050921371.html |access-date=2026-06-16 |website=Yahoo Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> The following game, Fox posted 7 points from 3-of-15 field goal attempts as the Spurs lost the series 4–1 to the Knicks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Anderson |first=Erik |date=2026-06-14 |title=San Antonio Spurs PG De'Aaron Fox Under Fire For Losing NBA Finals |url=https://heavy.com/sports/nba/san-antonio-spurs/deaaron-fox-stats-nba-finals-news/ |access-date=2026-06-16 |website=HEAVY |language=en-US}}</ref> Fox received additional criticism from fans and the media for his performance in the series in the context of his contract extension, averaging 12.8 points while shooting 34.4% from the field and 25% from the three-point line.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-06-15 |title=Spurs' De'Aaron Fox: Offensive nightmare in Finals loss |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/spurs-deaaron-fox-offensive-nightmare-in-finals-loss/ |access-date=2026-06-15 |website=CBS Sports |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Zucker |first=Joseph |title=De'Aaron Fox Reacts to Loss as Fans Troll Stats vs. Knicks Before $228.6M Spurs Contract Extension |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/25440319-deaaron-fox-reacts-loss-fans-troll-stats-vs-knicks-2286m-spurs-contract-extension |access-date=2026-06-15 |website=bleacherreport.com |language=en}}</ref>

==Player profile==
Listed at {{convert|6|ft|3|in|m}} and {{convert|185|lb|kg}},<ref>{{Cite web|title=De'Aaron Fox|url=http://www.nba.com/stats/player/1628368/|access-date=2021-04-14|website=NBA Stats|language=en}}</ref> Fox has primarily played the [[point guard]] position throughout his career. He is left-handed.

Coming out of [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], Fox was highly regarded among scouts for his quickness, speed, and athleticism.<ref>{{Cite magazine|last=Rollins|first=Khadrice|title=Who is De'Aaron Fox?|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2017/06/22/deaaron-fox-nba-draft-2017-scouting-report-analysis|access-date=2021-04-14|magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=June 22, 2017 |language=en-us}}</ref> These attributes combined make Fox one of the most dangerous players on the [[fast break]] and driving to the rim. Fox himself stated in 2018 "If we’re talking about from baseline to baseline with the ball in my hands, I’m definitely the fastest person in the league."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kalbrosky |first=Bryan |date=2018-12-22 |title=Kings' De'Aaron Fox has a point in saying he's the fastest NBA player |url=https://hoopshype.com/2018/12/22/sacramento-kings-deaaron-fox-fastest-nba-russell-westbrook-john-wall/ |access-date=2021-04-15 |website=HoopsHype |language=en-US}}</ref>

Fox is a high end finisher at the rim, being able to use his body control and leaping ability to finish [[layup]]s and draw fouls and often using his speed and quickness to blow by defenders. Fox is considered to be a poor [[Three-point field goal|3-point shooter]], as during the [[2019–20 NBA season|2019–2020 NBA]] season, Fox shot a career low 29.2% shooting percentage from three.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=De'Aaron Fox Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/f/foxde01.html|access-date=2021-04-14|website=Basketball-Reference.com|language=en}}</ref>

Fox has also demonstrated good passing ability, averaging around seven [[Assist (basketball)|assists]] per game.<ref name=":0" /> Fox generates most of his assists running the [[pick and roll]] and the fast break.

On defense, Fox can be exploited by bigger guards because of his small frame, but can intercept passes and makes quick rotations due to his elite quickness and nearly 6-foot 7 inch [[wingspan]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2017-05-12|title=2017 NBA Draft Combine Measurements|url=https://www.nbadraft.net/2017-nba-draft-combine-measurements/|access-date=2021-04-14|website=NBADraft.net|language=en-US}}</ref>

==Endorsements==
Fox signed a multi-year endorsement deal with [[Nike, Inc.|Nike]] prior to the [[2017 NBA draft]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=De'Aaron Fox {{!}} NBA Shoes Database|url=https://ballershoesdb.com/players/deaaron-fox/|access-date=2021-04-15|website=Baller Shoes DB|language=en-US}}</ref>

In October 2023, Fox signed a shoe deal with [[Curry Brand]], making him the first official signature athlete for the brand.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Benson |first1=Pat |title=De’Aaron Fox Signs Sneaker Deal with Curry Brand |url=https://www.si.com/fannation/sneakers/news/deaaron-fox-signs-sneaker-deal-with-curry-brand |website=Sports Illustrated |access-date=17 July 2025 |date=26 October 2023}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Fox was born to his parents Aaron and Lorainne Harris-Fox and has one brother named Quentin Fox. Since elementary school, Fox goes by the nicknames “Fox”, “Swipa”, and “Swipa da Fox”, inspired by Swiper the Fox from the [[Nickelodeon]] television series ''[[Dora the Explorer (TV series)|Dora the Explorer]]'' and his ability on the court to record steals.'''<ref name="c734">{{cite web | last=Duffy | first=Thomas | title=De'Aaron Fox Confirms 'Swipa' Nickname Is Inspired by 'Dora the Explorer' | website=Bleacher Report | date=June 21, 2017 | url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2717045-deaaron-fox-confirms-swipa-nickname-is-inspired-by-dora-the-explorer | access-date=March 1, 2025}}</ref>''' Fox chose the number zero at Kentucky because he “fears no one”, giving his original number five to teammate [[Malik Monk]], who played with him on the Kings. According to his high school coach, Fox would come to school at 6 AM and practice in the gym every morning. Fox would sleep on the couch almost every night and play the ''[[NBA 2K]]'' video game series. This, according to his father, is one of the reasons he has developed into the player that he is today.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2693422-how-kentucky-pg-deaaron-fox-is-teaching-himself-to-think-hoops-at-an-nba-level|title=NBA Draft 2017: How Kentucky PG De'Aaron Fox Is Teaching Himself to Think Hoops at an NBA Level|website=[[Bleacher Report]]|first=Reid|last=Forgrave|date=February 28, 2017|access-date=March 30, 2018}}</ref>

Fox is also a fan of the ''[[Dragon Ball Z]]'' [[anime]] series and says that [[Vegeta]] is his favorite character.<ref>{{Cite web|first=Andre|last=Key|date=March 7, 2018|title=Kings' De'Aaron Fox played Dragon Ball Z on Golden 1 Center's Big Screen|url=https://clutchpoints.com/kings-news-deaaron-fox-shows-photo-playing-dragon-ball-z-golden-1-centers-deaaron-fox-plays-dragon-ball-z-golden-1-centers-4k-big-screen/|access-date=2021-04-15|website=ClutchPoints|language=en-US}}</ref> In 2017, Fox sported ''Dragon Ball Z'' inspired [[Nike, Inc.|Nike]] shoes in game.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dunne |first=Brendan |date=July 27, 2017 |title=De'Aaron Fox Got Dragon Ball Z-Themed Nike Kobes |url=https://solecollector.com/news/2017/07/nike-kobe-ad-dragon-ball-z-deaaron-fox |access-date=April 15, 2021|website=Sole Collector |language=en}}</ref>

In February 2022, Fox was the subject of criticism after he shut down his personal [[Non-fungible token|NFT]] project “SwipaTheFox”, with more than $1.5 million in unpaid investment to approximately 100,000 investors. Fox explained his decision in a Twitter thread, wherein he claimed he wasn't satisfied with the quality of the project so far and was shutting it down until the end of the NBA season, but did not answer critics who demanded a return of their investment.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2022/2/25/22950186/deaaron-fox-defraud-nft-swipathefox-nba-kings|title=Did De'Aaron Fox really defraud people for $1.5M in an NFT 'rug pull' scheme?|last1=Dator|first1=James|website=[[SB Nation]]|date=February 25, 2022|access-date=April 27, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Fox |first=De'Aaron |date=February 24, 2022 |title=Twitter |url=https://twitter.com/swipathefox/status/1496949627077406721 |access-date=February 28, 2022}}</ref>

In August 2022, Fox married [[Recee Caldwell]] at an elaborate ceremony in Malibu, California.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Foglio |first1=James |title=Kings guard De'Aaron Fox weds Recee Caldwell in Malibu |url=https://www.basketballinsiders.com/news/kings-guard-deaaron-fox-weds-recee-caldwell-in-malibu/ |website=Basketball Insiders {{!}} NBA Rumors And Basketball News |date=9 August 2022}}</ref> Caldwell gave birth to their son Reign Fox on February 3, 2023.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Warnock |first1=Caroline |title=Recee Caldwell Fox, De'Aaron Fox's Wife: 5 Fast Facts You Need to Know |url=https://heavy.com/sports/dearon-fox-wife-recee-caldwell-fox/ |website=Heavy.com |date=27 April 2023}}</ref>
